{{nihongo|'''Tenmansha'''|天満社}} is a shrine in {{ill|Hachiōji|ar|هاتشيؤوجي (طوكيو)|arz|هاتشيؤوجى, طوكيو|azb|هاچی‌اوجی، توکیو|ban|Hachiōji, Tokyo|bg|Хачиоджи|ca|Hachiōji|ce|Хатиодзи|ceb|Hachiōji (lungsod sa Hapon)|cs|Hačiódži|da|Hachiouji|de|Hachiōji|eo|Haĉioĝi|es|Hachiōji (Tokio)|et|Hachiōji|eu|Hachiōji|fa|هاچیئوجی، توکیو|fi|Hachiōji|fr|Hachiōji|gl|Hachiōji|he|האצ'יוג'י|hy|Հաթիոձի|id|Hachiōji, Tōkyō|it|Hachiōji|ja|八王子市|ko|하치오지시|lt|Hačiodžis|mg|Hachiōji|ms|Hachioji|mzn|هاچی‌اوجی، توکیو|nl|Hachioji|no|Hachiōji|pl|Hachiōji|pt|Hachioji|ro|Hachiōji|ru|Хатиодзи|sh|Hachiōji|simple|Hachiōji|sr|Хачиоџи|su|Hachioji, Tokyo|sv|Hachiōji|tg|Ҳачиоҷи|th|ฮาจิโอจิ|tl|Hachiōji, Tokyo|tr|Hachiōji|tt|Хатиодзи|tum|Hachiōji|uk|Хатіодзі (Токіо)|ur|ہاچیوجی، ٹوکیو|vi|Hachiōji, Tokyo|war|Hachiōji|zh|八王子市|zh_classical|八王子市|zh_min_nan|Hatiôzi-chhī|zh_yue|八王子市|qid=Q208863}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tokyo}}. It is the origin of the place name {{ill|Kitanomachi|ja|北野町 (八王子市)|qid=Q11404303|lt=Kitano-chō}}. Its former {{ill|Shakaku|ja|社格|ko|사격 (신토)|zh|社格|qid=Q10444029}} was {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}}; this article also explains the subordinate {{ill|Shiogama shrine|Q133753|qid=Q133753|lt=Shiogama Shrine}}. {{nihongo|'''Tenmansha'''|天満社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Musashi Province]].
 
== History ==
* The founding is unknown; it is said a branch of the {{ill|Yokoyama-tō|Q11542517|qid=Q11542517}} invited {{ill|Kitano Tenmangū|Q662176|qid=Q662176|lt=Kyoto Kitano Tenmangū}} here<ref>'Hachiōji Naganuma-chō, Kitano-chō Wagamachi,' Masayuki Shimizu, Onkodō, 1987.</ref><ref>'Hachiōji Jiten,' Hachiōji Jiten no Kai, Katakura Shoten, 2001.</ref>.
* From {{ill|1591|Q6766|qid=Q6766}} ({{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}} 19) to {{ill|1860|Q7691|qid=Q7691}} ({{ill|Man'en|Q1193862|qid=Q1193862}} 1), it received 5 koku of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=sharyō}} land{{sfn|東京都神社庁}}.
* In the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}, prayer talismans for the shogun's military fortune were offered every year{{sfn|東京都神社庁}}.
* In the {{ill|1600s (decade)|Q42995|qid=Q42995}}, the sacred {{ill|Zelkova serrata|Q920344|qid=Q920344}} tree was planted.
* In {{ill|1664|Q7581|qid=Q7581}} ({{ill|Kanbun (era)|Q1146228|qid=Q1146228}} 4), shrine buildings were rebuilt.
* In {{ill|1880|Q7806|qid=Q7806}} ({{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 13), the shrine building with {{ill|Karahafu|Q977293|qid=Q977293}}-fronted portico was rebuilt.

== Sacred tree ==
The zelkova said to have been planted in the {{ill|1600s (decade)|Q42995|qid=Q42995}} still stands in the precincts.

Since the 2010s, branches of zelkova and cherry trees around the shrine perimeter extended over roads, and the city repeatedly gave {{ill|Administrative guidance|Q4683583|qid=Q4683583}} to prune them. In December 2019, the {{ill|Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism|Q1376196|qid=Q1376196}} also instructed pruning within that month, but there were no signs of compliance<ref>[https://www.asahi.com/articles/ASM9N3TFVM9NUTIL010.html?iref=com_rnavi_arank_nd04 Dangerous "sacred tree" even hides traffic lights: shrine's explanation for not removing it] - {{ill|The Asahi Shimbun|Q720503|qid=Q720503}}</ref>. On June 20, 2020, the MLIT Sōbu National Highway Office and Hachiōji City, under the Administrative Execution Act, forcibly cut protruding branches<ref>{{Citenews|title=Hachiōji City and the state conduct administrative execution to cut sacred tree: branches/leaves over roads, shrine ignored 22 rounds of guidance|url=https://mainichi.jp/articles/20200621/k00/00m/040/020000c|newspaper=Mainichi Shimbun|date=2020-06-21|accessdate=2020-06-21}}</ref>.

== Shiogama Shrine ==
Also called {{ill|Shiogama shrine|Q133753|qid=Q133753}}. It is famous as a shrine for abdominal-belt prayers for safe childbirth. It stands to the right of Tenman-sha.
